name: Sale and transfer of a leasehold title
summary: A registered lessee sells the unexpired residue of a lease. The instrument is LRA 63, and the lease's own terms decide what consent is needed before anything registers.
triggers: The title is leasehold, whether from the Government, a county or a private lessor
The transaction is a sale of the unexpired residue
The lessee is alive and transferring in their own right

not_this_if.why: LRA 33 transfers a freehold and section 55 does not bite.

not_this_if.fact: The lease is being given up rather than sold on
not_this_if.why: A surrender is LRA 65, not a transfer.

not_this_if.fact: A new lease is being granted
not_this_if.why: LRA 62, or LRA 64 for a long term.

statutory_basis.quote: the consent of the lessor has been produced to, and authenticated to the satisfaction of the
statutory_basis.effect: Where the lease restricts dealing, nothing registers until the lessor's consent is produced and authenticated. The section prescribes no form for that consent, which is why the plugin drafts it as a letter rather than a statutory form. That is correct here and would be wrong for a Land Control Board consent.

statutory_basis.quote: a land rent clearance certificate and the consent to the lease, certifying that no rent is owing to the Commission in respect of the land, or that the land is freehold, has been produced to the Registrar
statutory_basis.effect: The alternative route: a land rent clearance certificate together with the consent, certifying no rent owing to the Commission. This is what practitioners call the NLC or Commissioner of Lands consent.

statutory_basis.quote: a person executing an instrument shall
statutory_basis.effect: Verification of execution applies to a transfer of lease as to any other registrable instrument.

statutory_basis.quote: An instrument required by law to be stamped shall not be accepted for registration unless it is stamped

is void for all purposes unless the land control board for the land control area or division in which the land is situated has given its consent in respect of that transaction in accordance with this Act
statutory_basis.effect: Agricultural land within a land control area cannot be dealt with without the board's consent. Registration does not cure the want of it.

statutory_basis.quote: within six months of the making of the agreement for the controlled transaction
statutory_basis.effect: The clock runs from the agreement, not from completion. Six months, extendable only by the High Court for sufficient reason.

bundle.role: Application for the consent of the land control board, in the prescribed form
bundle.condition: The leased land is agricultural and within a land control area
bundle.why: Section 6(1) of the Land Control Act catches a lease and its transfer as readily as a sale of freehold.
Everything lodged goes under a general application.

bundle.condition: The leasehold title is charged and the charge is redeemed on completion
bundle.why: Registers before the transfer so the purchaser takes a clean residue.

bundle.role: Consent of the encumbrancer to the transfer
bundle.condition: The charge is not redeemed and the purchaser takes subject to it
bundle.why: Section 59 stops registration until the lender's written consent is produced.
The operative instrument. It passes the unexpired residue.

drafted_together.why: One lodgement on completion, the discharge registering before the transfer.

alternatives.decided_by: Whether the charge is redeemed on completion or survives it
alternatives.why: Both answer section 59 and only one is right for a given matter.

consents.name: Lessor's consent to the dealing
consents.when_required: The lease contains a condition against transferring without the lessor's written consent, which is the normal term
consents.when_not_required: The lease contains no such condition
consents.authority: The lessor, which for public land is the National Land Commission and for private land is the landlord
consents.consequence_if_missed: The dealing is not registrable. Section 55 has no prescribed form, so the consent is produced as a document and authenticated to the Registrar's satisfaction.

consents.name: Land Control Board consent
consents.when_required: The leased land is agricultural and within a land control area
consents.when_not_required: Urban or township land, or land outside a land control area
consents.authority: The land control board for the area
consents.consequence_if_missed: The transaction is void for all purposes.

consents.name: Lender's written consent, or a discharge
consents.consequence_if_missed: Nothing registers until it is produced.

clearances.name: Land rent clearance certificate
clearances.authority: the Ministry or the National Land Commission
clearances.when_required: Always on a leasehold where rent is payable. Section 55(b) names it expressly.

sequence: Read the lease itself before anything else. Its own covenant decides whether consent is needed and from whom.
Official search, so the encumbrances and the unexpired residue are known rather than assumed.
Establish whether the land is agricultural and within a land control area.
Obtain the lessor's consent and the land rent clearance certificate. On public land these come together.
Settle with the chargee: discharge or consent, not both.
Execute with section 45 verification, then lodge.

traps.trap: Treating the leasehold consent as the same thing as a Land Control Board consent
traps.why_wrong: They come from different authorities under different Acts, and only the Land Control Board consent has a prescribed form. A matter can need both.
traps.provision: Land Registration Act s.55 and Land Control Act s.6(1)

traps.trap: Selling more residue than the lease has left
traps.why_wrong: The unexpired term is a fact from the register and the lease, not from the client's recollection.

traps.trap: Leaving the land rent clearance certificate to the end
traps.why_wrong: Section 55(b) makes it part of what must be produced for the dealing to register, and it is slow to obtain.

practice_varies.note: For public land this has moved between the Commissioner of Lands, the Ministry and the National Land Commission. Record who your registry currently accepts.

practice_varies.step: Validity period of the rent clearance certificate
practice_varies.note: Varies. Record what your registry treats as current.
